01
Brand Foundation

An established
identity

Legacy Performance Institute is an elite performance institution. The identity carries that positioning in every mark, surface and interaction — assured, refined, and unmistakably its own. This is not a brand being advertised; it is a brand that already exists.

PremiumPerformance-DrivenInstitutionalRestrainedModernHuman
LPI combines the discipline of elite performance with the refinement of a premium institution and the warmth of a human community.
The Balance
  • Elite — without inaccessible.
  • Luxurious — without excessive.
  • Performance-focused — without generic hardcore-gym language.
  • Institutional — without becoming sterile.
  • Modern — without becoming trend-dependent.
  • Human — without losing authority.
Governing Philosophy
Confidence
through restraint.

The brand does not need to raise its voice. Space, precision and consistency carry more authority than volume ever could.

Supporting Idea
LPI should feel established,
not advertised.
02
Identity System

One system,
three configurations

A single, disciplined identity built for identification, recognition and specialized application. Each configuration has one job — choose it by what the moment requires, never by convenience. The primary lockup leads; the monogram and specialized lockup support.

Primary Identity

Legacy Performance Institute Lockup

Approved Standard
The default brand identifier. First-touch communications, website primary identification, formal documents, presentations, primary marketing, primary facility identification and external communications — anywhere the audience needs to understand who LPI is.
Full Lockup = Identification
Brand Monogram

LP Monogram

Approved Standard
Recognition and compact applications. Social profile images, favicons, apparel, hats, equipment, established social content, video watermarking, motion applications and secondary environmental branding — anywhere the brand is already established.
LP Monogram = Recognition
Specialized Lockup

Banner / Environmental Configuration

Approved Standard
A specialized production configuration for fascia, long-format signage, architectural applications, long interior walls, banners and constrained horizontal environments. It is not an alternative primary logo simply because horizontal space is available — use it only when architecture or production conditions justify it.
Use Only When Justified

Typographic Rules
  • Compose headlines with intentional line breaks — never leave them to chance wrapping.
  • A gold headline word is a rare, deliberate moment — never a default accent.
  • Numbered markers (01 / 02…) only where content is a genuine sequence or index.
  • Avoid all-caps beyond the defined micro-label system — no arbitrary capitals.
  • Institutional display is used sparingly; the editorial register carries the workload.
  • Hierarchy comes from scale, weight, tracking and space — not from decoration.
ProductionArchivo and Michroma are the web substitutes for the brand's specified faces. If Neue Haas Grotesk and Eurostile Extended are licensed, they replace these in the same roles — the system is unchanged. Substitute equivalents only where a platform cannot embed the licensed family.

Minimum clear space = 1X.

06
Core Visual System

The system,
in practice

The rules that govern how LPI looks and feels beyond the logo. Architecture, not ornament. Restraint, not volume.

Composition
  • Architectural grids
  • Generous negative space
  • Disciplined asymmetry
  • Clear hierarchy
  • Intentional alignment
  • Restrained information density
  • Editorial pacing — immersive, minimal, editorial, cinematic, informational
  • Hairline rules & controlled framing

Compositions are art-directed, not centered by default. Density varies deliberately — never two same-density blocks back to back.

Graphic Language
  • Fine structural hairlines
  • Circles & controlled frames
  • Corner devices
  • Geometry derived from the LP mark
  • Subtle oversized monogram applications

Graphic devices function as architecture, not ornament. Negative space is part of the identity.

Photography & Film

Grade — deep blacks, controlled highlights, cinematic contrast, slightly muted color, warm skin tones, architectural shadows, premium texture and selective black-and-white. All imagery reads as one campaign with a single grade. Athletes look focused, not performative. Coach portraits are black-and-white, desaturated by default with a subtle warm shift on interaction.

Scale — aggressive scale variety: full-bleed against small editorial crops, vertical editorial images, oversized architectural details, type overlapping image. Never repeat one ratio across a page.

Avoid — bright commercial gym lighting, stock fitness imagery, oversaturation, overprocessed HDR, bodybuilding clichés and people shouting at the camera.

Material Character
  • Obsidian & dark architectural surfaces
  • Charcoal
  • Dimensional lettering
  • Restrained metallic Legacy Gold
  • Warm neutrals, stone & glass
  • Rich Wood, leather & premium warm materials
  • Controlled lighting

The physical brand communicates permanence and sophistication.

MMotion BehaviorBehavior Standard
Motion — Vocabulary
  • Slow, controlled, precise — motion should feel expensive
  • One easing curve: cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)
  • Durations 800–1200ms on brand moments
  • Masked line-by-line text reveals
  • Opacity fades with a slight rise
  • Gold line expansion & subtle image scale
Motion — Restraint

Avoid bounce, elastic, overshoot, aggressive zoom and flashy transitions. Motion is an enhancement, never a dependency — always provide a reduced-motion fallback.

This deck demonstrates the standard: every reveal uses the brand easing at ~1000ms and collapses gracefully under reduced-motion.

This is not a normal gym.
This is a different standard.

Any surface built in this system should make a first-time visitor understand, within ten seconds and before knowing any price, that this is a different standard. If a composition doesn't pass that test, simplify it until it does.

Avoid excessive branding, repetitive logos, unnecessary gold, decorative logo effects, competing graphic elements, visual clutter and trend-driven treatments. LPI should feel established, not advertised.

BalanceHold roughly 70% luxury / editorial · 20% elite performance · 10% raw athletic intensity across the brand. Restraint is the strategy — negative space, hairlines, scale and the scarcity of gold carry the luxury, not decoration.

08
Signage & Environmental Direction

The brand in space

Phase 1 direction for how the identity should translate into physical space — establishing principles and character, not a completed facility rollout. The applications below are directional; specification, fabrication and facility design belong to a later phase.

Directional Study
Primary Identification

Full lockup, integrated

Primary facility identification uses the complete LPI lockup or the LP monogram, integrated into the architecture rather than applied as decoration. It sits in controlled negative space, at a scale governed by viewing distance and legibility — not maximized for its own sake.
Secondary Identification

LP monogram, restrained

The LP monogram handles secondary and wayfinding moments — restrained, occasional, never repeated as pattern. Recognition is the job; the brand is already established in the space.
Material & Light

Character, not specification

Dark architectural surfaces, dimensional lettering, restrained metallic gold, warm stone and wood, and controlled lighting. The material language communicates permanence and sophistication; branding stays restrained and the space carries the brand.
Obsidian & dark stoneDimensional letteringRestrained metallic goldWarm stone & woodControlled lighting
Governing Principle
The space carries the brand.
Branding stays restrained.
This section sets environmental character and standards only. No facility renderings or finalized signage treatments are presented as approved in Phase 1.

Logo Integrity
  • Use only the approved Legacy banner logo artwork.

Placement

Color

Production
